step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard architecture shows a data processing pipeline that begins with SQS receiving incoming event notifications. SQS triggers a Lambda function ('Job Initiator Lambda'). Lambda reads/writes configuration and state to DynamoDB. Lambda also triggers AWS Step Functions, which receives input/state from DynamoDB as well. Step Functions scales and orchestrates loading data into Amazon Neptune. Gremlin queries traverse Neptune and export graph output data to Amazon S3. Finally, AWS Glue catalogs the data stored in S3 for broad access.

graph.name: Homesite Insurance - Serverless Graph Database ETL Pipeline
graph.notes: Architecture uses SQS, Lambda, DynamoDB, Step Functions, Neptune, Gremlin, S3, and Glue to process customer web data into a graph database and export results to S3.

nodes.name: Glue
nodes.notes: Catalogs exported data in S3 for access via Athena
